line.name: Lampert 1675 Edición Morado
line.background_text: Edición Morado is a later entry in Lampert's 1675 series, produced for aficionados wanting a deeper, darker profile than the Azúl while retaining the brand's signature smoothness. Rolled at Fábrica AGROTABACOS in Nicaragua using tobacco aged 3-5 years. Treated as its own line entry (sibling to Azúl/Rojo within the 1675 series) since it has its own distinct wrapper/blend identity and dedicated product page, consistent with how the official site and retailers list it.

vitolas.summary_review: A medium-bodied smoke with mesquite and hickory smokiness balanced by milk chocolate and floral notes; rated 91/100 by Blind Man's Puff, though found somewhat one-dimensional by that reviewer.

critic_reviews.key_notes_text: 91/100; mesquite/hickory smokiness balanced by milk chocolate and floral notes; found somewhat one-dimensional.

research_notes: Confirmed distinct blend from Azúl/Rojo (different wrapper, darker/fuller profile). Robusto and Short Robusto dimensions not stated in sources checked - left null. Release year (2024) inferred from a secondary blog post, treat as approximate.
